value: This proposal is the smallest truthful bridge for the single RECOVERY01 hold 'started compose -> artifact_tail'. It covers an ART body that the original Step already committed, with the same key, the same immutable action and the same claim-epoch WorkRef. Managed recover finishes that same Step and attaches the body to the unchanged revision, so fresh VER under the fenced WorkRef can verify it and current readback shows it. Nothing new is added: no C15 call, reservation, Step charge, inference, save, Ref kind, Step field or VER change. If TSK-owned facts definitively forbid use, the Step is abandoned and the body remains ART history. Any uncertainty keeps the existing hold. Adoption grants no completion authority.
responsibilities: ART owns lookup_saved and all ART SQL. It rebuilds the canonical save input from {key,work_ref,step_id,action}, owns the not_found/unavailable/conflict/denied distinction, and gates its stored producer refs on the caller connection without writing. TSK changes only recover; ordinary finish_step and _authority stay unchanged. Within recover, TSK owns structural validation, intent classification, its source gate, comparison of the ART projection with the Step and call, the Step finish, the artifact-set row, the adoption row, the epoch fence, the single C14 event, replay, and the validator extension. VER is unchanged; fresh verification happens only later through normal execution. RUN performs no save, model call or reservation at startup; its save-key derivation must be the single function that TSK reuses. Root/SOL freezes these answers, wires ART and TSK on the same connection, owns the shared key-derivation binding, and owns the cross-owner tests.
contract_alignment: The proposal is consistent with these contracts. C08: key replay and immutable body. C09: fresh verification per WorkRef. In the supplied VER.verify, metadata is accepted for the same goal/revision with epoch <= current, and _current_status marks a verification invalidated when the artifact set is extended, so old receipts cannot complete. C13 recovery text: old-epoch ART may be recovery-adopted for the same revision when its sources are valid, and old VER is not reused. C14: the event is written in the same transaction. C15: no double charge. RECOVERY01: closed recover input, settled/held shapes, latest-intent order cancel > paused/pause flag > open question > queued, no regating for physical cleanup, gating for new adoption. The adopted Step passes the supplied _artifact_set and get_execution_context checks without change, because those checks are scoped by Goal/revision and allow older epochs: finished compose, sole artifact result, call.step link, record-only inputs with required <= inputs <= registered. ART inspect/_loaded already supply what lookup_saved needs: active-connection precondition, unique replay binding, binding_json, hash/bytes, UTF-8 re-preparation, and the producer gate under the savepoint guard.
evidence_limits: This is a design reading of the supplied text only; no tools, tests or hashes were used. Omitted TSK methods are not evidence. These include _authority, _finish_compose, _register, _registered, _gate/_check_sources, _event, _transaction, _remaining/_index, the ART authorize_save provider and the VER context provider. As a result, how ART orders recorded producer refs relative to call.sources, and where current_artifact_refs comes from, are unverified. The RECOVERY01 recover/register/finish_startup code, its lease/session/claim tables and its replay store are pending and are not evidence. The RUN save-key derivation and pal/artifact_content_v5 and artifact_integrity_v5 were not supplied; statements about them come only from the proposal text. I did not compute the declared excerpt source hash. I claim no source approval, test result, whole-C13, provider or product acceptance.
findings:
F1 ART, required. After a replay row is found, lookup_saved must not pass on _loaded's not_found. A receipt whose body row is missing is a dangling receipt and must return unavailable. not_found is definitive only when there is no v5_art_replay row for the key AND no v5_art_body row for the step_id (step_id is UNIQUE). These cases are unavailable: a body for the step_id whose key is absent, and a replay row whose body step_id or work_ref differs.
F2 ART. conflict means the stored input_json differs byte-for-byte from dumps({key,work_ref,step_id,content,media_type,source_refs}) rebuilt from the closed ComposeAction. save stored dumps of the loaded request, so order and duplicates are preserved. Comparing only the key, or comparing sets, is insufficient.
F3 Root/RUN/TSK. Only the proposal asserts that the save key is derived from the original WorkRef and step_id. TSK must call the same pure function RUN uses, not a copy, and a fixed case must check that both produce the same key. With F1 in place, key drift fails closed as a hold and never abandons a saved body.
F4 TSK. Compare the ART projection as follows: work_ref == Step.work_ref == call.work (the claim epoch, never the fenced epoch); step_id equal; artifact kind; record-only source_refs with no duplicates; set equal to call.sources; required <= sources <= registered. Require ordered equality only if authorize_save is shown to return call.sources verbatim. Because call.sources <= registered is already validated, 'register provenance' is an assertion and must not write.
F5 TSK. Add these eligibility checks: the linked call status is returned; the Step has empty result_refs and no error key; the stored action decodes as ComposeAction; the artifact_id appears in no artifact-set row and no adoption row.
F6 TSK. Make denied deterministic by fixing the order. TSK gates required plus call.sources once, before calling ART. denied there is definitive ineligibility; not_found or unavailable is a hold. If ART later returns denied or unavailable inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE after TSK saw available, that is an inconsistency and must hold.
F7 TSK. An adopted Step wire is identical to an ordinary finished tail, so a one-way annotation cannot detect deletion. Record the adopted step_id (or null) and the event_id in TSK's internal recover replay record, leaving the public settled value unchanged. The validator then checks the row and the replay reference against each other in both directions.
F8 TSK. Same-revision attach draining changes neither purpose nor conditions, so it is not ineligibility. Adoption must leave pending_inputs unconsumed. A valid open question alongside a running lease's started compose is inconsistent and gets an unavailable hold.
F9 TSK. Reuse RECOVERY01's single state event. When adopted, its refs are [artifact ref] and its text is fixed, with no body content or clock value. Ordinary finish paths add no progress or result event. Kind result is avoided because adoption is not completion. Abandon outcomes keep the existing event without the unattached artifact.
F10 Root. Pause non-adoption is a conservative policy choice, not something derived from source, because ordinary finish under pause_requested depends on the omitted _authority. I recommend accepting it: the body stays as ART history and the only cost is recomposition after resume, within existing ceilings.
recommendation:
REFINE: adopt the proposal with F1-F10 and freeze the four seam answers and fixed cases below.
S1 ART lookup_saved(connection,{key,work_ref,step_id,action}).
- Preconditions are identical to inspect: same connection object, active transaction, isolation_level None; otherwise raise ValueError.
- The request is closed and action must decode as ComposeAction; otherwise invalid_input.
- Order: (1) Read the replay row by key. (2) If absent: no body for the step_id gives not_found; a body gives unavailable. (3) If present and the canonical input mismatches: conflict. (4) Run _saved_receipt. (5) Run _loaded on the row's artifact ref; not_found becomes unavailable; the projection work_ref and step_id must equal the request. (6) Gate the stored producer refs under the existing savepoint guard.
- Results: available gives success {artifact_ref,work_ref,step_id,hash,bytes,source_refs} carrying the original WorkRef; denied gives denied; not_found or unavailable gives unavailable.
- Exception gives unavailable; BaseException propagates after savepoint cleanup.
- No BEGIN/COMMIT, writes, content return, authorize_save, id or clock; total_changes stays unchanged.
S2 TSK, recover only.
- No collaborator means the existing hold. Ordinary finish_step and authority are unchanged.
- Order: full RECOVERY01 validation, then intent class, then TSK gate, then ART lookup, then the F4/F5 comparison, then writes. All of it runs in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with preminted ids.
- Adoption writes: the original Step wire with status finished, result_refs [artifact ref], the original work_ref and no new keys; one artifact-set row at the next seq; lease close and latest epoch+1 fence as in RECOVERY01; one row v5_tsk_recovery_adoption(step_id PK, call_id UNIQUE, lease_id UNIQUE, artifact_id UNIQUE, origin_work_json, adopted_work_json, recover_key, event_id UNIQUE); replay; event.
- Budgets, call, reservation and ART rows are untouched.
- Validator (_artifact_set plus recovery validation), per adoption row: the Step is a finished compose whose result is exactly that artifact; Step.call == call_id; call.step == step_id; call.lease == lease_id; call.status is returned; call.work == Step.work_ref == origin == the lease claim WorkRef; same goal/revision as adopted; adopted epoch > origin epoch and equals that recover replay's settled work_ref; the set row exists exactly once; the event exists with refs [artifact]; the replay references this step. Conversely, every replay adoption reference must have its row. An ordinary finished compose with no row and no reference remains valid history.
S3 Event and replay.
- One existing RECOVERY01 state event, per F9, inside the settlement transaction.
- A same-key replay returns the stored settled value and adds no event, epoch or row.
- The artifact is visible only through Step result_refs, the current artifact set/C02 current_artifact_refs, and the execution context.
- No new Ref, Step, Result or settled-value fields.
S4 Ineligibility.
- TSK-owned definitive ineligibility skips the ART lookup and the source gate, but never structural validation. Cases: latest revision differs, latest state is terminal or has cancel intent, or the work is paused or has a pause flag. In each case, abandon the Step without adoption and settle by latest intent. A TSK gate denied is handled the same way.
- After lookup: not_found means abandon and settle, with no re-save and no model call. denied applies only as in F6.
- conflict, unavailable, invalid_input, an exception, or a comparison mismatch all keep the held artifact_tail with no writes, replay, epoch or event.
Fixed cases.
ART:
- A1 exact match succeeds with zero changes and no body returned.
- A2 no key and no body gives not_found.
- A3 a dangling receipt, a body without a key, and a foreign step body each give unavailable.
- A4 changed content, media type, order or duplicates give conflict.
- A5 tampered hash, bytes, UTF-8 or binding gives unavailable.
- A6 gate denied versus gate not_found/unavailable map as specified.
- A7 wrong or idle connection is refused.
- A8 a gate collaborator that writes or commits gives unavailable; BaseException propagates.
TSK:
- T1 adopt once with the exact rows and unchanged counters, including when the budget is exhausted.
- T2 replay adds no event or epoch; a different input gives conflict.
- T3 not_found abandons.
- T4 each hold source leaves zero writes, and a later retry adopts.
- T5 change, cancel, terminal, pause, pause flag and TSK-denied each abandon; an ART spy is not called and the body is intact.
- T6 F4/F5 mismatches hold.
- T7 a tampered or missing adoption row, replay reference or set row gives unavailable, while ordinary history stays valid.
- T8 no collaborator holds.
- T9 premint failure or BaseException at each write rolls back.
Root:
- R1 real ART+TSK+VER on temporary SQLite: crash after ART COMMIT, then recover adopts; fresh VER with a new key accepts the old-epoch metadata; the old receipt is invalidated and cannot complete.
- R2 crash before COMMIT abandons, and the next claim uses a fresh call within ceilings.
- R3 pause, change, cancel or source-stop committed through a second connection before recover never adopts.
- R4 RUN and TSK derive the same key.
- R5 HOST tests are unchanged, with no startup save, model call or reservation.
Root checks these points against the integrated code; no blanket second review is required.
